raw_response:
I will still do my wheat-maize rotation on the full 3 mu, same as before. I have only 3 mu, so every bag of fertilizer is money, but I will not cut too hard on fertilizer and risk yield. Around here, if wheat base fertilizer is too light, tillering is poor and the ears are small later; if maize is short of fertilizer at jointing, the stalk stays thin and the cob does not fill well. I usually start from what I did last year and then adjust a little. With well irrigation in my field, I can push yield a bit more steadily than dryland, so I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed. For wheat, I will put more fertilizer in the base and then topdress once at the greening-jointing stage, with 3 irrigations if the season is normal. For maize, I will put some fertilizer at sowing and the main nitrogen at big bell mouth or before tasseling, with 2 irrigations if rain is not enough. I watch what nearby farmers do too. Most people here do not dare starve the crop, especially on such a small plot. I will also keep 2 pesticide sprays for each crop in mind, because one bad disease or insect spell can cost more than the spray money.
